blank6_name_sec2 = | blank6_info_sec2 = | blank7_name_sec2 = | blank7_info_sec2 = | short_description = | footnotes = }} '''Quezon''', officially the '''Municipality of Quezon''' ({{langx|tl|Bayan ng Quezon}}), is the titular [[municipality of the Philippines|municipality]] in the [[Philippine Province|province]] of the [[Quezon|same name]]. According to the {{PH wikidata|population_as_of}}, it has a population of {{PH wikidata|population_total}} people.{{PH wikidata|population_reference}} The municipality was named after [[Manuel L. Quezon]], the second [[Presidents of the Philippines|President of the Philippines]], first President of the [[Commonwealth of the Philippines|Philippine Commonwealth]], and the former governor. It is home to the recently started Yubakan Festival and a few speakers of the critically endangered [[Inagta Alabat language]], one of the most endangered languages in the world as listed by [[UNESCO]]. ==History== Prior to the establishment of the municipality of Quezon, its area was inhabited by the Dumagat people, who primarily lived along the coast. In 1672, [[Franciscan order|Franciscan]] friars led by Tirso de Santa Maria explored the area and established a village, which eventually grew into a place called ''Silangan'', from the [[Tagalog language|Tagalog]] word meaning [[east]], signifying the direction where the sun rises. The town faced challenges, including pirate attacks, prompting the establishment of stone fortifications, including those at [[Gumaca]]. On January 1, 1914, eleven barrios were excised from [[Alabat, Quezon|Alabat]] to officially form the new municipality of Quezon, by virtue of Executive Order No. 101 signed by [[Governor-General of the Philippines|Governor-General]] [[Francis Burton Harrison]] in 1913. The municipality was named after [[Manuel L. Quezon]], the then-[[Resident Commissioner of the Philippines|Resident Commissioner]] and a former [[Governor of Quezon|governor]] and native of the province then known as Tayabas. Barrio Silanga (Silangan) was designated as the seat of municipal government.{{cite web |url=https://quod.lib.umich.edu/p/philamer/ACD6603.1913.001?rgn=main;view=fulltext |title = Executive orders and proclamations issued by the governor-general. [1913]}}{{cite web|url=https://quezonquezon.gov-ph.net/history-of-municipality-of-quezon-province-of-quezon/|title=History of Municipality of Quezon, Province of Quezon|website=Official Website of the Municipality of Quezon, Quezon|accessdate=March 30, 2024}} ==Geography== Quezon is located at the southeastern tip of [[Alabat Island]], which is accessible to the rest of Quezon through a sea route via [[Gumaca]] and eventually the under-construction [[Roma Point Bridge]]. ===Barangays=== Quezon is politically subdivided into 24 barangays, as indicated below. Each barangay consists of [[purok]]s and some have [[sitios]].
